To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the semantic properties in the lower conceptual domains of regular ERDs can be completely described by their fundamental functional dependencies, and a large number of regular ERDs have equivalent underlying relational structures.
the lower conceptual domain contains the semantic information which helps determine the data representation power of an ERD.

the lower conceptual domain contains a large amount of information, that fundamental FDs can be readily recognized in the lower conceptual domains of ERDs, that fundamental FD can be derived in polynomial time from the fundamental FDs of the underlying relational structure, that the set of all fundamental FDs in an ERD can be derived in linear time from the set of all FDs in the underlying relational structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of translating ERDs into relational structures.
the problem of determining the data representation power of ERDs and the relationship between ERDs and relational structures.
the problem of how to translate the semantics of ERDs into the semantics of relational structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lower conceptual domain is a key factor in the translation of an ERD into a relational structure.
an entity-relationship diagram is equivalent to a relational structure if and only if it is regular and its underlying relational structure has a unique representation.
the lower conceptual domain contains a significant portion, and in some cases all, the semantic information of the ERD, and that this portion is essential to the data representation power of the ERD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lower conceptual domain plays a significant role in determining the data representation power of an ERD.
we have shown that the lower conceptual domain plays a key role in determining the semantic properties and the data representation power of an ERD.
the lower conceptual domain plays a crucial role in determining the data representation power of an ERD.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fundamental FDs are a good basis for the translation of an ERD into a relational structure, and the translation can be done by using a set of fundamental FDs that are present in the lower conceptual domains of the ERDs.
a significant portion of an ERD's semantic information can be captured by a small number of fundamental FDs.
, in general, the relational structure underlying an ERD does not fully represent the information contained in the ERD.
